root_cause.text: `vti6_tnl_lookup()` in `net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c` failed to verify wildcard endpoint state when doing fallback lookups in the shared `ip6n->tnls_r_l` hash table, so hash collisions could make it return a non-wildcard tunnel that merely matched one address field.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds the missing checks `ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.raddr)` for the “local address” fallback and `ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.laddr)` for the “remote address” fallback, and the commit message states these loops “were missing checks to ensure that the candidate tunnel actually has a wildcard address.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict VTI6 tunnel lookup to tunnels with an unspecified remote address so only the intended tunnel is matched.
intent_record.what: In `vti6_tnl_lookup()`, the tunnel match condition was extended by adding a check that `t->parms.raddr` must be the IPv6 unspecified address (`ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.raddr)`) in addition to matching the local address and having the device up.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the lookup will now only return a VTI6 tunnel when its remote address is unset/any, preventing tunnels with a configured remote IPv6 address from being selected by this code path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict VTI6 tunnel lookup to tunnels with an unspecified local address so only the intended tunnel is selected.
intent_record.what: In `vti6_tnl_lookup()`, an additional condition `ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.laddr)` was added to the tunnel match inside the RCU tunnel iteration.
intent_record.how: The lookup now returns a VTI6 tunnel only when the remote address matches and the tunnel's local address is unspecified, in addition to the device being up. This prevents tunnels with a configured local IPv6 address from being selected by this lookup path.

candidates.rationale: This fallback lookup only checked the local address and device state, but did not verify that the tunnel's remote endpoint was wildcard/unspecified. As a result, a hash collision in the shared tnls_r_l table could return a non-wildcard tunnel that matched only one address field.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit fbe68ee87522f6eaa10f9076c0a7117e1613f2f7
Author: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
Date:   Thu Nov 20 10:01:49 2014 +0100

    vti6: Add a lookup method for tunnels with wildcard endpoints.
    
    Currently we can't lookup tunnels with wildcard endpoints.
    This patch adds a method to lookup these tunnels in the
    receive path.
    
    Signed-off-by: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>

diff --git a/net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c b/net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c
index d440bb58552
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body already includes the wildcard-endpoint lookup paths added by the commit. After the initial exact hash lookup, it explicitly tries `hash = HASH(&any, local);` and matches only `ipv6_addr_equal(local, &t->parms.laddr)` for local-wildcard tunnels, then `hash = HASH(remote, &any);` and matches only `ipv6_addr_equal(remote, &t->parms.raddr)` for remote-wildcard tunnels. This is the intended fix for the reported issue. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause—falling back in `ip6n->tnls_r_l` without verifying wildcard endpoint state, allowing a hash collision to return a non-wildcard tunnel—is not present in this snippet as a bug; instead the code separates wildcard lookups and checks the matching endpoint field before returning.
